P301 subject screening index

32,098 subject IDs across 99 sites. 30,415 are in the V03 randomized population. A full screening date is recorded for 32,097 IDs.

Screening date is the start date (SVSTDTC) of the visit named Screening. Previous and unscheduled screening dates are separate fields in the CSV. “SV only” means the ID appears in screening records but not in this BLA ADSL; it does not assign a reason for non-randomization.

Source: FDA-CBER-2022-1614-3824347-3825106_125752_S3_M5_mrna-1273-p301_A_D_adsl.jmp and FDA-CBER-2022-1614-4188701-4201848_125752_S3_M5_mrna-1273-p301_S_sv.jmp. Companion CSV

Does the number increase by one?

98/99 (98.99%) of sites begin at the assumed start, 2001. Other first observed suffixes: US361 (2003).

  • Subjects: 31,952/32,098 (99.55%) either have the first site number 2001 or are exactly one higher than the preceding observed ID at that site.
  • Increments only: 31,854/31,999 (99.55%) are +1 when each site’s first observed ID is excluded.
  • Positions occupied: 32,098/32,281 (99.43%) from 2001 through each site’s last observed ID.

183 missing positions in the BLA screening index: 181 internal gaps in 145 jumps at 59 sites, plus 2 leading positions under the assumed start of 2001. No positions are inferred beyond the last observed number.

Of all missing positions: 36 orange are recorded in EUA ADSL (36 not randomized; 0 randomized); 2 purple are recorded in BLA DM only; and 145 red are absent from both comparison rosters.

Largest internal gap: US370, suffixes 2055 through 2088 (34 numbers between 2054 and 2089).

Strict uninterrupted sequence and source checks

If every suffix must equal 2001 plus its zero-based row number within its site, 19,666/32,098 (61.27%) match. A skipped number affects all later ranks; it affects only one adjacent increment. These statistics describe numeric order, not the chronology of screening or ID assignment.

As a separate chronology check, 139 of 31,997 adjacent observed pairs with two screening dates have the higher ID screened earlier. 28,146 pairs were screened on the same day; their order within that day is unknown.

Of the internal gaps, 36 IDs are recorded in the EUA ADSL (0 flagged randomized); 4 are recorded in the BLA demographics table (DM), including 2 in both. This confirms 38 identifiers in at least one comparison roster. The other 143 were not found in those two rosters. A skipped number alone does not establish that a person enrolled or that a record was deleted.

Beyond a site’s last indexed ID, the reference rosters independently contain: US3712311. These are documented identifiers outside the range, not inferred gaps, and are excluded from the counts above.

Reference snapshots: P301 EUA ADSL (25 Nov 2020) and original production S3 DM. Membership is checked against full reference rosters, not a roster of flagged IDs. The screening index itself is the union of the March 2021 BLA ADSL and screening-related SV records.

Reading the highlighted rows: Orange means the identifier was found in EUA ADSL, whether or not it is also in BLA DM; the row gives its recorded randomization flag. Purple means it was found in BLA DM but not EUA ADSL. Red means it was found in neither comparison roster. Internal gaps and assumed leading positions are distinguished by their row labels. Each highlighted row is absent from the BLA screening index; it has no imputed screening date and does not increase the subject count. The filters never create new gaps.
